Carrier Tracking Numbers: Formats, Checksums & Parsing

11 min read Updated: November 2026 By Rajvardhan Singh Rathore
Every global carrier encodes security and validation digits into their tracking numbers. Learn how to parse, sanitize, and execute mathematical checksum verification against FedEx, UPS, USPS, and ocean container numbers.

Carrier Tracking Format Architecture

Tracking numbers are not arbitrary strings; they contain structural carrier codes, service tier identifiers, account numbers, package sequential sequences, and a final mathematical check digit:

  • UPS: 18 characters beginning with 1Z (e.g., 1Z9999999999999991). Uses Modulo-10 on character numeric equivalents.
  • FedEx Express: 12 digits (e.g., 794612345678). Uses weighted Modulo-11 with weights [3, 1, 7, 3, 1, 7, 3, 1, 7, 3, 1].
  • FedEx Ground: 15 digits or 20 digits (SSCC-18 compliant).
  • USPS: 22 digits starting with 9400, 9205, or 9300.
  • Ocean Container (ISO 6346): 4 letters (3 owner + 1 category) + 6 digits + 1 check digit (e.g., MSKU1829304).

UPS 1Z Modulo-10 Checksum Algorithm

The UPS 1Z check digit is calculated across characters 3 through 17:

  1. Letters are converted to numbers: A-Z map to $(( ext{ASCII} - 63) \pmod{10})$.
  2. Odd position digits (1-indexed) are summed.
  3. Even position digits are multiplied by 2 and summed.
  4. The total sum modulo 10 is subtracted from 10 (or 0 if remainder is 0).

FedEx 12-Digit & 15-Digit Mod-11/Mod-7

FedEx Express 12-digit barcodes multiply the first 11 digits by repeating weights (3, 1, 7, 3, 1, 7, 3, 1, 7, 3, 1). The remainder modulo 11 determines the check digit (if 10, check digit is 0).

Ocean Container ISO 6346 (BIC) Check Digit Calculation

Every shipping container in the world conforms to ISO 6346. Each character is mapped to an international value, multiplied by $2^i$, summed, and evaluated modulo 11.

Unified Python Checksum Verification Engine

Python Checksum Engine 
def verify_fedex_12(tracking: str) -> bool:
    if not tracking.isdigit() or len(tracking) != 12:
        return False
    weights = [3, 1, 7, 3, 1, 7, 3, 1, 7, 3, 1]
    total = sum(int(digit) * weight for digit, weight in zip(tracking[:11], weights))
    check = (total % 11) % 10
    return check == int(tracking[11])

def verify_iso6346_container(code: str) -> bool:
    code = code.strip().upper()
    if len(code) != 11:
        return False
    char_map = {
        'A': 10, 'B': 12, 'C': 13, 'D': 14, 'E': 15, 'F': 16, 'G': 17, 'H': 18, 'I': 19,
        'J': 20, 'K': 21, 'L': 23, 'M': 24, 'N': 25, 'O': 26, 'P': 27, 'Q': 28, 'R': 29,
        'S': 30, 'T': 31, 'U': 32, 'V': 34, 'W': 35, 'X': 36, 'Y': 37, 'Z': 38
    }
    total = 0
    for i, ch in enumerate(code[:10]):
        val = char_map[ch] if ch in char_map else int(ch)
        total += val * (2 ** i)
    check_digit = (total % 11) % 10
    return check_digit == int(code[10])
